Build an Ordinal-Regression Learner Adapter (Experimental)

Source: R/learner_ordinal.R
make_ordinal_adapter.Rd

Returns a closure that fits ONE elastic-net cumulative-logit model (ordinalNet) on a single bootstrap subsample and returns a logical selection mask over the features, mirroring the role of make_glmnet_adapter() for ordered outcomes.

Usage

make_ordinal_adapter(alpha = 1)

Arguments

alpha

Numeric in (0, 1]; the elastic-net mixing weight inside ordinalNet. Default 1 (pure lasso).

Value

A function with signature function(x, y, lambda_val) -> logical vector of length ncol(x) for use inside stabl_fit(), where lambda_val is a 1-row data.frame from the lambda grid (see auto_ordinal_lambda_grid()).

Selection rule

With parallelTerms = TRUE the proportional-odds model gives one slope per feature. A feature is selected at a grid row when the absolute value of its slope exceeds the same small coefficient cutoff the glmnet adapters use. The grid is a lambda path (see auto_ordinal_lambda_grid()); lower penalties give supersets of the selections at higher penalties, so the stability-accumulation and FDP+ logic in stabl_fit() work unchanged.

Statistical guardrails (read before using)

  • Outcome type. y must be a factor; its level order is the band order. An ordered factor is recommended. Numeric outcomes must be banded by the caller (for example with cut()).

  • Experimental. This learner is an extension beyond Python STABL and has no Python-parity counterpart. FDP+ calibration for the ordinal learner is validated by the WS-9 simulation benchmark; consult the benchmark summary before treating FDP+ as calibrated.

  • Decoys. Artificial features are outcome-agnostic; both random_permutation and model-X knockoffs apply unchanged.

Calibration status (experimental)

Simulated calibration evidence (10 seeds x 2 proportional-odds designs) shows knockoff_equi mean FDP+ of 0.00 (nominal 0.1) but mean TPR of only 0.37 on both designs – the learner is strongly conservative and did not meet the predeclared graduation bar. It stays experimental; see benchmarks/ws9_summary.md.

See also

auto_ordinal_lambda_grid(), make_glmnet_adapter(), stabl_fit()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ordinalNet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1L)
  x <- matrix(rnorm(400L), 40L, 10L,
              dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("f", 1:10)))
  eta <- x[, 1] - 0.5 * x[, 2]
  y   <- cut(eta + rnorm(40L, sd = 0.5), breaks = 4,
             labels = paste0("L", 1:4), ordered_result = TRUE)
  grid   <- stablr:::auto_ordinal_lambda_grid(x, y, n_lambda = 5L)
  adapter <- stablr:::make_ordinal_adapter()
  mask <- adapter(x, y, grid[1L, , drop = FALSE])
  cat("selected at sparsest lambda:", sum(mask), "of", ncol(x), "\n")
}
#> selected at sparsest lambda: 0 of 10
